A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CD-MoE work. Their complete text, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including v2's Appendix A. Material relocated from v1's main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original DeepSeekMoE and Qwen pruning experiments, fine-tuning results, selection ablations and calibration-data analysis.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original compression and fine-tuning outcomes, ablations, runtime measurements and layerwise metric analyses.

M1.justification: The condensation algorithms and fixed gates are unchanged; updating only condensed layers was already specified in v1. The limited procedural revision concerns the reported recovery workflow: v1 Section 4.3 explicitly uses language modeling followed by SFT, while v2 describes task SFT and no longer documents the language-modeling stage.

E1.justification: Training coverage changes from the reported C4 language-modeling stage plus commonsense170k to commonsense170k and explicit MMLU supervised training. Both retain C4 calibration and the same eight zero-shot benchmarks. Qwen evaluation was already present in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds a distinct comparison family: GPT-Neo-2.7B, OPT-2.7B, BLOOM-3B and OpenLLaMA-3B appear with scores in Tables 1 and 7. BlockTrim, LayerTrim and the selection-ablation comparators remain; Layer Rank and Global Layer Rank rename existing methods.

E3.justification: Fine-tuning evaluation changes from a six-task commonsense average to an eight-task average including RTE and MMLU. The stated learning rate changes from 5e-5 to 1e-4, and inference/fine-tuning hardware from a 48GB A40 to an 80GB A100. Appendix A also corrects the calibration-question total from 200 to 160 and DeepSeek's activated-expert count from six to eight; these corrections do not establish resampling or architectural changes.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds layerwise KL-divergence and perplexity profiles alongside the existing JS analysis. Table 3 expands runtime analysis with inference counts and estimated exhaustive-search costs. Existing expert-selection, layer-selection, metric-selection and calibration-data analyses remain, although L3 columns disappear from two ablation tables.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix A.2 newly states that all experiments used a single run because of resource limits. V1 gives no corresponding run-count disclosure. This adds transparency without establishing a change in repetitions; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds dense-baseline scores, per-task SFT results averaging 59.1 and 60.5, and detailed Qwen results. Retained DeepSeek CD-MoE zero-shot rows are unchanged, but LayerTrim's eight-layer MMLU score changes from 30.8 to 29.8 and its average from 49.5 to 49.4. L3 ablation entries are removed. The fine-tuning results use revised conditions and are not directly comparable across versions.

T1.justification: The MoE output equations, calibration-averaged gates, JS/KL definitions and Hill estimator are mathematically equivalent. JS and KL formulas receive equation numbers in v2, but no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central condensation contribution remains. The headline operating point changes from approximately 30% memory reduction and 30% faster inference to 27.5% reduction and 1.26x speed. V2 also strengthens the previously qualitative fine-tuning benefit into an explicit claim of recovering 98% of original performance within five A100 hours.

C2.justification: V1's direct-SFT instability warning and LM+SFT explanation disappear. V2 emphasizes recoverable knowledge in retained experts, attributes Qwen's stronger retention to its larger shared-expert fraction, and softens the limitation for architectures without shared experts. Its new blanket claim that statistical expert-selection baselines never outperform greedy search exceeds the evidence in Table 2.

D1.justification: V2 adds PyTorch/Transformers implementation information, exact model parameter counts, trainable-parameter fractions and SFT durations. The code-access information remains unchanged. Some detail is lost: v1 explicitly instructs applying softmax to outputs before JS comparison, whereas v2 omits that instruction.

R1.justification: V2 removes the separate general LLM-pruning discussion and associated citations, including OWL and dynamic-sparsity work, while adding ShortGPT and references accompanying the dense-model comparisons. The central positioning against expert pruning and whole-layer trimming remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. V2 adds contribution bullets, renames the variants CD-MoE-S/SR, reorganizes implementation and supplementary material into Appendix A, and creates separate Limitations and Potential Risk sections.

P2.justification: V2 adds an architecture diagram, redraws the JS line plot as bars, combines the previously separate DeepSeek and Qwen plots into Figure 3, and restructures the fine-tuning plots. Plot ranges, legends and captions change substantially. Tables gain activated-parameter columns, grouped SFT comparisons and expanded appendix displays.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the practical claims easier to assess through per-task SFT and Qwen tables, dense-model comparisons, runtime details and single-run disclosure. It also corrects inconsistent calibration and expert counts. These gains are limited by the unexplained omission of the earlier LM stage and a new overstatement: Table 2 still shows PL_Alpha_Hill beating greedy search at L6, 56.8 versus 56.5. Overall, documentation and evidential clarity improve modestly.
